items.title: For a locally Noetherian integral scheme, UFD local rings are equivalent to normality together with surjectivity of the Picard to class group map
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a locally Noetherian integral scheme, having unique factorisation domain local rings is equivalent to being normal with surjective Picard to class group map, in which case that map is an isomorphism (statement lines 6907-6918). The counted proof has two real halves: the first direction combines normality with the fact that prime divisors are effective Cartier divisors to get injectivity and surjectivity of the class group map, and the second direction uses a surjectivity hypothesis to realize a given prime divisor as the divisor of a meromorphic section and then, at each local ring, constructs an element of the fraction field with order one at a chosen height one prime and order zero elsewhere, concludes it lies in the local ring, shows every element of that prime is a multiple of it, and applies the criterion that a Noetherian normal domain with principal height one primes is a unique factorisation domain (proof lines 6920-6953). It is H2: both directions are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard normality, divisor and unique factorisation criteria.
